D.treatment: dc-bias reasoning when analyzing input signals

O.outcome_detail: distinguishing dc bias behavior from small-signal behavior

cells.quote: After all instruction on transistors, the majority of students gave responses that did not address the small-signal behavior of the circuits. Instead, the most common lines of reasoning were appropriate only for finding dc voltages.
cells.note: This is an authors' cross-task interpretation of written-response patterns, not a randomized comparison or a tested instructional treatment.

D.treatment: comparing common-emitter amplifiers by small-signal gain
D.comparison: comparing them by dc bias voltages and resistor voltage drops

O.outcome_detail: understanding signal-amplitude behavior of BJT amplifier circuits

cells.quote: Failure to differentiate between signal and dc bias. After all instruction on transistors, the majority of students gave responses that did not address the small-signal behavior of the circuits. Instead, the most common lines of reasoning were appropriate only for finding dc voltages.
cells.note: The study reports descriptive response patterns without an inferential comparison or effect size.

D.treatment: comparing output at the collector and emitter (circuits B and C)
D.comparison: comparing circuits with exchanged collector and emitter resistors (circuits B and A)

O.outcome_detail: correct pairwise comparison of peak-to-peak output voltages

cells.quote: Of students who compared circuits B and C, approximately 75% correctly found that Vout,C < Vout,B, with a spread between 66% and 86% of students giving correct comparisons in each course. There was substantial variation in students’ comparisons of circuits B and A, with the correct ranking (Vout,B > Vout,A) given by between 30% and 60% of students in a given course.
cells.note: The text shows higher descriptive performance for the B-versus-C comparison, but reports no inferential test or effect size.

D.treatment: targeted questions about fundamental transistor behavior
D.comparison: complex comparison of three amplifier circuits

O.outcome_detail: understanding and explanation of BJT circuit behavior

cells.quote: However, students often displayed knowledge of fundamental transistor behavior when responding to more targeted questions. On the three amplifier comparison task, the majority of the students struggled in their efforts to rank all three circuits according to the amplitudes of the peak-to-peak output voltages.
cells.note: This is a task-complexity contrast described narratively; no direct effect size or inferential comparison is reported.
